skill.name: brainstorming
skill.description: Transform rough ideas into detailed designs through structured dialogue before implementation begins.
skill.summary: Guide early product and engineering ideas into validated design documents through structured questioning.
skill.author: DMJGilbert

security_audit.summary: All eight static findings are false positives caused by markdown fences or ordinary design-process guidance. No prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, or malicious behavior was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: Markdown fences were flagged as shell backtick execution.
remediation.suggestion: No security fix is required. Keep code fences clearly labeled as documentation examples.

remediation.issue: Post-design guidance asks the agent to save and commit a design document.
remediation.suggestion: Ask for user confirmation before creating files or committing repository changes.

static_findings.snippet: **Key rule:** One question at a time - avoid overwhelming

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 38 opens a fenced markdown example for option formatting. It is documentation text, not Ruby execution or a shell command.
Line 52 closes the fenced markdown example started at line 38. The backticks delimit documentation and do not execute commands.
Line 83 opens a fenced markdown example comparing weak and strong questioning styles. No executable command or interpolation is present.
Line 94 closes a markdown documentation fence. It is not Ruby shell backtick execution.
Line 109 opens a fenced markdown template for a design document. It contains placeholder prose, not executable code.
Line 140 closes the design document markdown fence. The backticks are formatting syntax only.
The text says to ask one clarifying question at a time. It does not request host, network, account, or environment reconnaissance.
The line advises considering hybrid design approaches. It has no system discovery, probing, or sensitive data collection behavior.

content.value_statement: Unclear feature ideas often cause rushed builds and missed requirements. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code create validated design plans.
actual_capabilities: Guides one-question-at-a-time requirement discovery before implementation.
Compares two or three solution approaches with trade-offs.
Applies YAGNI thinking to reduce speculative scope.
Builds design sections for architecture, components, data flow, errors, and tests.
Keeps the plan open to revision through incremental validation.
Produces a structured design document after the idea is validated.
limitations: It does not implement the final feature by itself.
It relies on the user to answer clarifying questions accurately.
It cannot guarantee that all hidden constraints are discovered.
Saving or committing design files should require explicit user approval.

use_cases.title: Shape a New Product Feature
use_cases.description: Clarify goals, users, constraints, and success criteria before a team commits to a build path.

use_cases.title: Compare Engineering Approaches
use_cases.description: Explore several technical options and choose the simplest design that meets current needs.

use_cases.title: Prepare Implementation Handoff
use_cases.description: Turn a validated concept into a concise design document with components, data flow, tests, and open questions.

prompt_templates.title: Clarify a Rough Idea
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the brainstorming skill to help me refine this idea: [describe idea]. Ask one clarifying question at a time.

prompt_templates.title: Explore Solution Options
prompt_templates.scenario: Compare approaches before selecting a design.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the brainstorming skill to present two or three approaches for [feature]. Lead with your recommendation and explain trade-offs.

prompt_templates.title: Reduce Scope for MVP
prompt_templates.scenario: Narrow a large idea into a practical first version.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the brainstorming skill to identify what belongs in the MVP for [project]. Challenge speculative requirements and defer nonessential work.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Validated Design
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for a complete pre-implementation design.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the brainstorming skill to guide me from requirements through a final design document for [feature]. Validate each section before continuing.

output_examples.input: We need a new onboarding flow, but the team has not agreed on details.
output_examples.output: The skill asks what success means for onboarding, then compares simple, guided, and personalized flows before drafting a scoped design.

output_examples.input: I want to add notifications to our app.
output: First question: what user event should trigger the notification?
After clarification, the skill outlines components, delivery rules, error handling, and test coverage.

output_examples.input: Our feature plan has too many possible additions.
output_examples.output: The skill separates required MVP behavior from deferred enhancements and records open questions for later review.

best_practices: Start with the business goal and the user impact before discussing architecture.
Answer each clarifying question directly so the design can stay focused.
Review every proposed trade-off before asking the agent to produce the final design.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for implementation before the requirements are validated.
Do not approve a broad design that includes speculative future features.
Do not let the agent save or commit files without explicit confirmation.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps turn rough ideas into clearer requirements, solution options, and design documents before implementation.

faq.question: Does it write production code?
faq.answer: No. It is designed for planning and design refinement before coding starts.

faq.question: Can it work with existing projects?
faq.answer: Yes. It can review project context and ask targeted questions about constraints and patterns.

faq.question: How does it prevent overbuilding?
faq.answer: It applies YAGNI guidance and challenges features that are not required for the current MVP.

faq.question: Can teams use it for design reviews?
faq.answer: Yes. Teams can use it to compare approaches, document trade-offs, and record open questions.

faq.question: Should it commit files automatically?
faq.answer: No. File creation and commits should happen only after the user gives clear approval.
